summary:
ASTRA Observatory is an integrated astronomical research platform combining astronomical image processing, stellar photometry, and exoplanet analysis. Built using React, Python, and scientific libraries such as Astropy, Photutils, and Lightkurve, it aims to simplify the analysis of real astronomical observations, initially focusing on NASA's TESS datasets. Its modules support FITS image inspection, stellar brightness measurement, light-curve processing, and transit-signal analysis. With an emphasis on scientific accuracy, uncertainty estimation, and reproducibility, ASTRA aims to make advanced astronomical data analysis more accessible to students and researchers.

Founder & Lead Developer: Shankhalin Ghosh

ASTRA OBSERVATORY

Intelligent Astronomical Research & Scientific Computing Platform

Founder & Lead Developer: Shankhalin Ghosh

ASTRA Observatory is an ambitious, modular astronomical research and scientific computing platform designed to make advanced astronomical data analysis more accessible, efficient and reproducible.

Its primary objective is to bridge the gap between complex astronomical datasets and meaningful scientific interpretation through computational intelligence.

ASTRA integrates two principal research engines:

ASTRA VISION focuses on astronomical image processing, FITS inspection, celestial-object detection, image-quality assessment and visual analysis.

ASTRA EXO specialises in exoplanet research through stellar photometry, light-curve processing, transit-like signal detection, orbital-period estimation and transit modelling.

Its supporting infrastructure, ASTRA CORE, manages scientific computation, data validation, uncertainty propagation and reproducibility.

The platform aims to integrate authentic NASA datasets, particularly observations from the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS), alongside reference information from established astronomical archives.

Powered by scientific computing technologies including Astropy, Photutils, NumPy, SciPy and Lightkurve, ASTRA prioritises mathematical accuracy, transparent methodologies and independently verifiable results.

Its long-term potential extends towards automated astronomical workflows, multi-mission dataset integration, advanced celestial-object classification, collaborative research environments and institutional scientific applications.

ASTRA is envisioned as an open scientific software ecosystem with potential institutional services, serving students, independent researchers, universities and professional astronomers.

Its ultimate ambition is to transform astronomical data into accessible, reproducible scientific knowledge while contributing meaningful computational tools to the broader aspect
